summary: Iteration 5 (IberoAcademy certificate approval flow). Backend: 21/21 pytest tests passing in test_iteration5.py (serial, -n 0 — class-scoped fixtures share state so xdist loadscope with 2 workers races on admin seed; must run with -n 0). Covered: (a) passing final exam creates diploma status 'pendiente' with code matching ^IBA-[A-Z2-9]{4}-[A-Z2-9]{4}$ and submit response includes diploma_code; (b) while pending — public verify 404, public PDF 404, owner PDF 404; (c) GET /api/diplomas lists the pending record for admin; (d) RBAC: student→403, docente→403 on approve; (e) admin approve returns status 'aprobado', approved_at, verify_url; second approve→400; (f) after approval — owner GET /api/diplomas/{code}/pdf returns application/pdf starting with %PDF, other student→404, staff ok, public PDF ok, public verify returns student_name/course_title/code/approved_at; (g) PDF text extracted via pymupdf contains student full name, course title, 'Maximiliano Alcafuz Orellana', 'Liliana Hernández Guerrero', 'Karolyne González Possamai', 'Directora Académica', and the approval code; PDF has ≥1 image (QR); (h) reject pending→200 (status 'rechazado'), reject already-approved→400; (i) GET /settings has directora_name='Karolyne González Possamai'; (j) POST /settings/certificate-preview returns a PDF with the default template, with a custom PNG template uploaded via /api/files + settings PUT (then reset); (k) invalid verify code→404. Frontend smoke-test: minted admin+student JWTs. /diplomas (admin) → tab diplomas-tab-pending → certificate-request-<id> row + certificate-approve-<id> button visible; clicking approve switches diploma to issued. /diploma/{code} (student) renders diploma-document iframe + diploma-code 'IBA-XFX3-JPQN' + diploma-download-button. /verificar/{code} (no auth) renders verify-student-name='TEST_i5uiStu UI', verify-code='IBA-XFX3-JPQN', verify-download-pdf link pointing to /api/public/diplomas/{code}/pdf. /configuracion (admin) renders settings-directora-name=Karolyne González Possamai, settings-directora-signature-input, settings-certificate-template block with 'Usando la plantilla IberoAcademy (diseño del ZIP adaptado)', settings-template-input, and settings-certificate-preview (preview opened in new tab — the browser tool's networkidle wait timed out on the PDF viewer but the popup was triggered and the backend preview endpoint returns PDF — tested directly in backend suite). Backend logs: no 'Certificate request email failed', 'Certificate email failed', 'Certificate render failed' or 'Certificate preview failed' entries. The real owner admin (ed0.2580@gmail.com) was temporarily set active:false during tests and restored to active:true afterwards.
critical_code_review_comments: approve_diploma issues the PDF synchronously inside the HTTP handler (pymupdf render + external put_object). pymupdf's render_certificate uses asyncio.to_thread so the event loop isn't blocked, but a slow object store PUT keeps the admin request hanging. Consider moving the PDF generation+upload entirely to BackgroundTasks and returning immediately with 202 (status='procesando'), then flipping to 'aprobado' once the PDF upload completes. Today a timeout mid-approve leaves the diploma pending without surfacing the error cleanly to the admin.

build_certificate_pdf fetches rec from db.files without checking rec is None — if an admin uploads a template, then deletes the file via some other path, approving a diploma would throw TypeError. Add a 404 fallback or validate before generating.

notify_admins_certificate is launched via asyncio.create_task(...) in a request handler (issue_diploma on final-exam submit). If the loop closes before the task runs or if there are many enrollments, exceptions are only logged with a generic message. Prefer BackgroundTasks like in approve_diploma for consistency and to avoid 'coroutine was never awaited' type footguns.

cert_approved_email_html exposes the full approval code and a direct public verify URL in email body. Fine today, but note the public PDF endpoint has no rate limiting — anyone who scrapes the pattern IBA-XXXX-XXXX can brute-force codes (~10^7 keyspace with 4+4 chars from 32-char alphabet gives ~1.1T, so brute force is OK, but add basic rate limits on /public/verify/{code} and /public/diplomas/{code}/pdf to be safe).
approval_code generation lacks a retry on DuplicateKeyError. The diplomas.code unique index would raise 500 on an (astronomically unlikely) collision. Wrap insert_one in a loop with up to 3 retries.

backend/pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope. For this new suite tests share module-scoped fixtures (admin, settings_snapshot, seed, diploma_pending) and class fixtures that mutate state across classes — must be run with '-n 0' (serial). Document in pytest.ini or split fixtures to be fully isolated per-class to make xdist safe.

verify_diploma (public) returns the student RUT. Consistent with the attendance-cert flagged previously — exposing Chilean national IDs on a public verify endpoint is a privacy risk. Consider masking (e.g., '12.345.***-9') or omitting.

DiplomaView.jsx — the useEffect cleanup only revokes URL for the pdfUrl created in the SAME render; if pdfUrl state is captured in closure, URL.revokeObjectURL is called only once and the local `url` var captures value at mount. Works today but will leak Blob URLs if `code` changes between renders without unmount. Prefer revoking the previous pdfUrl in a dedicated effect keyed on pdfUrl.

Settings.jsx preview() PUTs the whole settings object before calling preview — but the preview endpoint already reads live settings. If the PUT fails (e.g., signature too large), the user sees a generic toast but has silently persisted a partial change. Separate the save from preview.

server.py reject_diploma allows rejecting a diploma that was already 'rechazado' (silently updates reject_reason). Not a bug per se, but UI shows 'Rechazar' button only for non-rechazado items; backend should be idempotent-strict (400 on second reject) for symmetry with approve.
